request.user:
Subject: Physics
Question type: single-correct (exactly one option is right)

What should be the approximate kinetic energy of an electron so that its de-Broglie wavelength is equal to the wavelength of X-ray of maximum energy, produced in an X-ray tube operating at 24800 V ? (given that h = 6.6 × 10^(− 34) joule-sec, mass of electron = 9.1 × 10^(− 31) k g )
(A) 600 eV
(B) 365 eV
(C) 120 eV
(D) 300 eV

result.working: The X-ray of maximum energy has the minimum wavelength: λ = hc/(eV) = 12400 eV·Å / 24800 eV = 0.5 Å. The electron must have the same de-Broglie wavelength, so p = h/λ = 6.6×10^-34 / 0.5×10^-10 = 1.32×10^-23 kg m/s. KE = p²/(2m) = (1.742×10^-46)/(1.82×10^-30) = 9.57×10^-17 J. Dividing by 1.6×10^-19 J/eV gives about 598 eV ≈ 600 eV.
